"Defenders also need to make use of AI and respond proactively, staying one step ahead." Emergency shutdowns this week from Tokyo to Helsinki of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services marked one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running. Companies including brokerage Nomura, lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, airline ANA and East Japan Railway (JR East) temporarily suspended some internet services as part of emergency measures. Japan's Ministry of Finance, National Tax Agency and Meteorological Agency also suspended some online services. On Friday, JR East said some group services had resumed while others would be restored once confirmed safe. Nippon Paint said it had applied a security patch as a precaution and its website is back online. Attackers are likely targeting Japanese businesses for their thorough records, which are no longer protected by a language barrier because of AI, said Eva Chen, CEO of Trend Micro.       Japan has been too comfortable with its existing infrastructure, which it felt was safe enough, she said. Cybersecurity experts have said AI is helping attackers automate tasks from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect. The developers of PHP - a computing language like HTML and Python - released fixes on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI. They urged users to "update immediately".

Source: Reuters

item.title: 仏暴動で風当たり強まる極左ＬＦＩ、各政治勢力が党首を批判
item.description:
Michel Rose Elizabeth Pineau
[パリ ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Michel Rose　Elizabeth Pineau

[パリ ２２日 ロイター] - フランスで近年最悪規模とされる暴動が発生したことを巡り、中道左派から極右までの政治勢力が、急進左派「不屈のフランス（ＬＦＩ）」と党首ジャンリュック・メランション氏（７５）への批判を強めている。同氏やＬＦＩが長年続けてきた対決的な政治姿勢が社会の緊張を高め、現在の混乱につながったとの主張だ。

メランション氏は５月に４度目となる大統領選出馬を表明し、左派候補として来年の大統領選決選投票への進出が最有力視される。ただ、複数のフランス都市で暴動が発生して以降は逆風にさらされている。

ルコルニュ首相は２０日、ＬＦＩについて「暴力と混乱を国に植え付けるという党の政治的な狙いが今や明らかになった」と語った。

これに対してメランション氏は、暴動の責任はＬＦＩにあるとの見方を否定。政府こそが貧困層の多い郊外地域での根深い社会・経済問題への対応を怠ってきたと反論した。

それでもＬＦＩへの批判は政治的立場を超えて広がっている。上院議長ジェラール・ラルシェ氏は今週の有力紙フィガロで、ＬＦＩを禁止すべきかどうかを検討する価値があるとの考えを示した。そのほか極右政党「国民連合（ＲＮ）」のローラン・ジャコベリ広報担当者はＬＦＩを含む極左勢力と「制御不能な移民政策」が、革命的な風潮を生み出したと主張。中道政党「民主運動」のマルク・フェノー氏は、メランション氏が長年にわたって「あらゆることを闘争の場に持ち込まなければならない」との考え方を広めてきたと指摘した。

フェノー氏はロイターに「全てを対立構図に変えてしまえば、大きなリスクを招く」と語った。

一連の批判は、メランション氏が依然として有力なフランス政治家の１人であると同時に、同氏が国内で強い警戒感を呼んでいることを浮き彫りにしている。次期大統領選を控えてフランスは今後、勢いを増す反体制勢力と弱体化した中道勢力との対立が焦点となる見通しだ。

今回の暴動はその構図を一層鮮明にしており、急進左派へ向けられる目が厳しさを増す半面、ＲＮの事実上の指導者マリーヌ・ルペン氏には治安・法秩序問題でより大統領候補らしい姿勢を打ち出す機会を与えている。治安問題は伝統的に極右勢力に有利な争点とされる。

一方フランス政界はなお極右、中道、左派の力が拮抗し、いずれも単独で主導権を握れない以上、メランション氏は引き続き相応の存在感を示すとみられている。

item.title: ロレアル、第3四半期売上高が予想上回る 高級美容品が需要けん引
item.description:
Dominique Patton
[パリ ２２日 ロイター] - フランスの化粧品大手ロレアルが２２日発表した第３・四...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ロレアル、第3四半期売上高が予想上回る　高級美容品が需要けん引 14:12 配信

ロレアルのロゴ。２０２１年５月、パリ近郊ルヴァロワ・ペレのオフィスで撮影。REUTERS/Christian Hartmann

Dominique Patton

[パリ ２２日 ロイター] - フランスの化粧品大手ロレアルが２２日発表した第３・四半期決算は、売上高が調整後既存店ベースで前年同期比７．７％増の１１５億６０００万ユーロ（１２９億５０００万ドル）となり、伸びはビジブル・アルファがまとめたアナリスト予想平均の５．９％増を上回った。高価なヘアケア製品や高級スキンケア製品に対する購入意欲が追い風となった。

ロレアルはスキンケア製品「セラヴィ」やイタリアのブランド「プラダ」の香水を手がけている。近年はプレミアム商品の展開に力を入れており、大ヒットを誇る有名ブランドのラインアップに高級香水を追加するとともに、ヘアサロン向けブランド「ケラスターゼ」から新たなヘアケア製品を展開している。

同社の高級化粧品部門はグループ売上高全体の３分の１以上を占めている。第３・四半期の既存店売上高は前年同期比７％増となり、市場予想の４．５％増を大幅に上回った。中国における高級スキンケア製品や、「プラダ・パラダイム」などの売れ筋香水への堅調な需要に支えられた。

同社は化粧品と香水の両部門における強固な事業基盤により、高級ブランドへの需要が加速している中国を含め、世界的に拡大する美容関連消費の恩恵を受けている。

二コラ・イエロニムス最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は声明で「世界の美容市場は、厳しい状況下においても再び回復力を証明した。当社は引き続き市場平均を大幅に上回る成長を維持した」と述べた。

item.title: ドイツ、税収見通し上振れ 財務相「財政余地は拡大せず」
item.description: ［ベルリン ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ベルリン　２２日　ロイター］ - ドイツのクリングバイル財務相は２２日、同日公表した新たな税収見通しについて、今後数年間の税収は従来予想を小幅に上回る見込みだが、財政余地の拡大にはつながらないとの見方を示した。その上で「将来の政策対応の余地を確保するため、連邦財政の健全化を続ける必要がある」と語った。

税収推計を担う専門家会議の最新予測によると、２０２６─３０年の税収は５月時点の予想を４３４億ユーロ（４８６億ドル）上回る見通し。財務省によると、増収分の多くは州や地方自治体に帰属し、このうち連邦政府の取り分は５年間で３３億ユーロにとどまる。

同省は税収見通しの上振れについて、欧州最大の経済大国である同国で長年の停滞を経て景気回復の兆しが出ていることが背景にあると説明した。

専門家会議はまた、２７年の連邦政府の税収が５月時点の予想を４１億ユーロ上回ると見込んでいる。ただ、この予測には議会による承認待ちの減税措置は織り込まれていない。

クリングバイル氏は議会で審議中の予算案に言及し、「良いニュースは、新たな財源不足が生じないことだ。悪いニュースは、新たな財政余地も生まれないことだ」と述べた。

item.title: 米朝首脳の年内会談、実現の可能性低下 米韓当局者が見方
item.description:
Trevor Hunnicutt David Brunnstrom Antoni Slodkowski Ju-min Park
[ワシントン／北京 ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Trevor Hunnicutt　David Brunnstrom　Antoni Slodkowski　Ju-min Park

[ワシントン／北京 ２３日 ロイター] - 米国と韓国の当局者は、トランプ米大統領と北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記が年内に会談する可能性が低下しているとみている。事情に詳しい関係者５人が明らかにした。

北朝鮮の指導者と会談した唯一の米大統領であるトランプ氏は、北朝鮮との対話再開に意欲を示している。しかし、北朝鮮は核開発計画の抑制を目的とする外交にほとんど関心を示していない。

関係者らによると、米国は首脳会談の開催について北朝鮮から回答を得ておらず、会談の機会となり得る１１月の中国での地域首脳会議まで時間がほとんど残されていない。５人のうち４人は米韓の高官から説明を受けた関係者で、残る１人は韓国当局者。

金氏の妹で、強い影響力を持つ金与正党総務部長は、両首脳の関係は「極めて良好」と述べているが、北朝鮮国営メディアは、同国が首脳会談に応じるにあたり厳しい条件を設ける構えで、制裁緩和などが含まれる可能性があると伝えている。

トランプ氏は８月、年内に金氏と会談する計画だと述べ、金氏が自身の働きかけに応じたと説明していた。

韓国の情報機関は９月下旬、１１月１８─１９日に中国・深圳で開かれるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議に合わせて両氏が会談する可能性は５０％だと国会議員らに伝えた。

しかし、トランプ氏は今月１９日、ＡＰＥＣ首脳会議や、同じく１１月にフィリピンで開かれる地域首脳会議の際に会談が実現する可能性について、慎重な見方を示した。

item.title: Volvo Cars shares in record plunge on widening losses, job cuts
item.description: Volvo Cars shares fell almost 30% on Friday after the Swedish carmaker posted a far bigger-than-expected third-quarter operating loss and said it would cut a further 2,500 jobs, mostly in its home market Sweden.
item.dc:creator: Marie Mannes
item.content:encoded: Volvo Cars (VOLCARb.ST) shares fell almost 30% on Friday after the Swedish carmaker posted a far bigger-than-expected third-quarter operating loss and said it would cut a further 2,500 jobs, mostly in its home market Sweden. The slump, which takes the shares deeper into record lows, comes as the firm, majority-owned by China's Geely Holding (GEELY.UL), struggles with uneven demand for electric vehicles, mounting tariff pressures and tough market conditions in China. "The third quarter of 2026 was very disappointing and reflects a year that has become far more challenging than originally anticipated. Our ongoing turnaround plan therefore needs a decisive reinforcement," CEO Hakan Samuelsson said. The automaker reported an operating loss of 3.7 billion Swedish crowns ($373 million) in the quarter, versus a profit of 5.8 billion crowns a year earlier. Citi analysts said the consensus forecast was for a loss of 724 million crowns. CEO Samuelsson returned from retirement in 2025 on a two-year contract to turn Volvo around. But despite [USN:L8N3R60KQ TEXT:"harsh"] cost cuts, a regionalisation plan and closer Geely ties, the outlook has only worsened. The carmaker said it needs to trim another 5 billion crowns of costs. The latest measures will affect about 6% of Volvo's workforce, including around 2,000 jobs in Sweden, through the termination of consultant contracts, natural attrition and targeted exit packages, it said. The cuts come in addition to 3,000 job reductions previously announced. Samuelsson told Reuters that the cuts should be completed by mid-2027, although he did not rule out further measures. INCOMING CEO FACES DEEPENING CRISIS Former Skoda boss Klaus Zellmer, who will succeed Samuelsson next year, will need to stem the decline of one of Europe's most well-known car brands. "Zellmer... has an even harder job on his hands now than when he was announced one month ago," Bernstein analysts wrote in a note, saying they struggled to see things improving any time soon. Volvo's [USN:L6N3Y80UT TEXT:"EX60"], an electric version of the best-selling XC60 and central to Volvo's turnaround, has been hit by heavy delays due to issues with battery assembly. Only around 5,000 units of the planned 40,000 for this year have been [USN:S8N40K029 TEXT:"built so far"], the company said. The company [USN:L6N45O0BV TEXT:"scrapped its guidance"] for full-year sales volume and cash flow this month, saying it would prioritise margins over market share in its key market in China rather than join an intensifying price war with domestic rivals, as its third-quarter revenue fell nearly 50%. Volvo's gross margin fell to 14.7% in the third quarter from 20.4% a year earlier, it said. Six of the 13 models Volvo plans to launch by the end of the decade will be designed for China and Samuelsson does not see any improvement in the group's performance there until they start arriving, he said. "We should have maybe realised earlier that we need to be more regional in China, maybe we should have also realised earlier that tariffs would come so we need to localise more in the US," Samuelsson said. "So that's a weakness right now which we are addressing." ($1 = 9.9180 Swedish crowns)

item.title: 米ロードアイランド州がメタ提訴、詐欺広告を容認したと主張
item.description:
Jeff Horwitz Katie Paul
[２２日 ロイター] - 米ロードアイランド州は２２日、「フェイスブッ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ロードアイランド州がメタ提訴、詐欺広告を容認したと主張 14:07 配信

メタのロゴ。２０２５年６月、パリのポルト・ド・ヴェルサイユ展示場で撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

Jeff Horwitz　Katie Paul

[２２日 ロイター] - 米ロードアイランド州は２２日、「フェイスブック」、「インスタグラム」、「ワッツアップ」の各プラットフォーム上で詐欺広告を容認したとして、メタ・プラットフォームズを州裁判所に提訴した。

ネロンハ州司法長官は、メタが数十億ドル規模の詐欺広告の作成に加担し、そこから不法に利益を得ていたと非難。同社は数十億人のユーザーに対し、ユーザー保護のために懸命に取り組んでいると保証していたにもかかわらず、このような行為を行っていたとしている。

米国の州がメタを相手取って提起した初の詐欺関連訴訟となる。５月にはカリフォルニア州サンタクララ郡が同様の訴訟を提起した。

訴状では、州法違反の各事案に対する民事制裁金、消費者への賠償、不正に得た利益の返還に加え、プラットフォーム上で作成・配信する詐欺広告から利益を得るのではなく、これに対処するようメタに命じることを求めている。

「訴状で主張されている通り、メタは脆弱なユーザーを詐欺に故意にさらし、それによって莫大な利益を得た。大小を問わず、企業がロードアイランド州の消費者を搾取する場合、当オフィスは権限の範囲内であらゆる手段を講じて、その責任を追及する」とネロンハ氏はプレスリリースで述べた。

一方メタは、この訴訟を「根拠がない」として争う意向を示し、同社が詐欺ネットワークを摘発するために法執行機関と定期的に連携していると主張。広報担当者は「州司法長官は、ロードアイランド州民を詐欺から守るための当社の取り組みについて協議することを拒否し、その代わりに州外の民間法律事務所を雇い、われわれが日々詐欺対策として行っているあらゆる取り組みを無視した訴訟をでっち上げた」とする声明を出した。

メタが過去１年間だけで１億５９００万件以上の詐欺広告を削除し、フェイスブックでの不審な友達リクエストを警告するアラート、広告主の認証プロセスの拡充、ワッツアップでの危険なデバイス連携リクエストに関する警告など、新たな詐欺対策ツールを導入したと強調した。

item.title: 仏ケリング、主力ブランド「グッチ」売上高6％減 再建計画に打撃
item.description:
Tassilo Hummel Alessandro Parodi
[パリ ２２日 ロイター] - フランス高級ファッシ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
仏ケリング、主力ブランド「グッチ」売上高6％減　再建計画に打撃 14:04 配信

グッチの衣装。5月16日、米ニューヨークで撮影。REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz

Tassilo Hummel　Alessandro Parodi

[パリ ２２日 ロイター] - フランス高級ファッショングループのケリングが２２日発表した２０２６年第３・四半期決算は、主力ブランドであるイタリアの「グッチ」の売上高が前年同期比６％減の１２億９０００万ユーロ（１４億４０００万ドル）となった。昨年就任したルカ・デメオ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）の指揮下での急速な成長回復への期待は打ち砕かれた。

グループ全体の売上高は１％減った。発表を受け、ケリングの米国預託証券（ＡＤＲ）は１１％下落した。

デメオ氏は利益率倍増を目指す５カ年計画でケリングの立て直しを図っている。しかし、混迷する中東情勢、中国での需要低迷、米国での勢いの鈍化が壁となっている。

アルメル・プールー最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）はメディア向けの電話会議で、年内に全体的な成長軌道への復帰が今も目標なのかとの質問に、通期決算の発表を理由にしてコメントを差し控えた。

ケリングによると、グッチの主な問題は特に中国における客足の減少で、同ブランド売上高は３年以上にわたり減少を続けている。北米でもグッチの売上高はわずかに減った。

プールー氏は「当社は最大限の規律を持って計画を続ける」と強調。これまでに小売店舗網を１０５店舗削減しており、来年末までに１２５店舗の閉鎖を目指していると表明した。

デメオ氏はコスト削減、さらなる店舗閉鎖、サプライチェーン（供給網）の合理化を推進することで利益率を２５年の１１．１％から２０年代末までに倍増させることを目指している。ただアナリストは、ブランドの魅力を失った事業を立て直すには単なる効率化対策だけでは不十分だと指摘している。

item.title: スウェーデン中銀、ＣＢＤＣ導入議論再開呼びかけ 通貨競争力懸念で
item.description: [ストックホルム ２２日 ロイター] - スウェーデン中央銀行（リクスバンク）は、新たなデジタル決済手段の普及やユーロ圏...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
スウェーデン中銀、ＣＢＤＣ導入議論再開呼びかけ　通貨競争力懸念で 13:59 配信

[ストックホルム ２２日 ロイター] - スウェーデン中央銀行（リクスバンク）は、新たなデジタル決済手段の普及やユーロ圏での取り組みなどを背景に、中央銀行デジタル通貨（ＣＢＤＣ）「ｅクローナ」の導入を巡る議論を再開すべきとの見解を示した。

スウェーデンは世界で最もキャッシュレス化が進んだ国の一つで、リクスバンクは国民が現金からカードやデジタル決済へ移行する中、ブロックチェーン技術を活用した小売向けＣＢＤＣの導入を検討した先駆的な中央銀行の一つだった。ただ、２０２３年の政府調査では、スウェーデンでのＣＢＤＣ導入の緊急性は高くないとの結論を示していた。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）がデジタルユーロ導入計画を進める中で、リクスバンクは議会に対して再検討するように求めている。

リクスバンクのヤンソン副総裁は２２日のロイターの取材に対して「スウェーデンは現金利用が極めて少ない社会であり、それは重要な意味を持つ。現金がデジタル化される一方で、スウェーデンクローナが使いやすいデジタル形態で提供されなければ、国境を越えて容易に利用できる他の便利なデジタル決済手段との競争に勝てなくなる可能性がある」と述べた。

リクスバンクが今年実施した調査によると、直近の買い物で現金を利用したスウェーデン人はわずか５％だった。

また、リクスバンクは今月の議員宛ての書簡で、ステーブルコインの発展がクローナの国際競争力に影響を与える可能性にも言及。クローナの利用が縮小した場合、中銀は金融政策の波及経路の維持や金融システムの安定確保で課題に直面する恐れがあるとしている。

ＥＣＢは２９年にもデジタルユーロを導入する可能性がある。ヤンソン氏は、リクスバンクとしてｅクローナに関する立場をまだ決定しておらず、最終判断は議会に委ねられると説明しつつも、必要な法整備や準備には少なくとも５年を要するとの認識を示した。

その上で「スウェーデンがデジタルクローナを導入し、他国に大きく後れを取らないようにするのであれば、今から準備作業を始めるのが望ましい」と訴えた。

item.title: 国内債は妙味次第で積み増し、最大500億円程度＝大樹生命・26年度下期運用計画
item.description:
Atsuko Aoyama
［東京 ２３日 ロイター］ - 大樹生命保険は２３日、２０２６年度下期の超長期債投資に...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
国内債は妙味次第で積み増し、最大500億円程度＝大樹生命・26年度下期運用計画 13:47 配信

写真は日本円紙幣。10月20日、東京で撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Atsuko Aoyama

［東京　２３日　ロイター］ -   大樹生命保険は２３日、２０２６年度下期の超長期債投資について、低利回り債から高利回り債への入れ替えを積極的に進める方針を示した。計画としては国内債券の残高を横ばいとしているものの、妙味次第で為替ヘッジ付外債から国内債へのシフトを検討する考え。上期は簿価ベースで９００億円の積み増しを実施し、下期も最大で５００億円程度と見積もっており、年度では最大１４００億円規模の積み増しとなる可能性がある。同社の運用統括部長の為我井心氏が運用説明会で語った。

為我井氏はＡＬＭ推進を目的とした超長期債投資について、ヘッジ外債と比べた妙味で「国内債の方が強いと判断した場合には、上期同様、ヘッジ外債から国内債へのシフトを検討していきたい」と述べた。上期には国内債を積み増した９００億円分、ヘッジ外債が減少した。

オープン外債は引き続き減少の計画。上期は１００億円の減少だった。株式は横ばいとし、投資妙味に応じた入れ替えを検討する。上期は５０億円の増加。

貸付は減少の見通しで、利回りやＥＳＧ面での厳選投資を継続。上期実績は２００億円の減少となった。オルタナティブ投資は上期実績が５０億円の増加。下期も増加の計画で、ダイレクトレンディング・ＰＥを中心とした積み増しを継続する。

日銀の金融政策については、来年１月と７月の２回の追加利上げを予想。ターミナルレート（利上げ最終到達点）は１．７５％と想定する。 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は年内に１回の追加利上げを行うとみている。

足元では株安や米金利の低下などリスクオフの動きがみられるが、そうしたリスクオフの影響は「今のところ一時的とみている」（為我井氏）という。

２０２６年度末の市場見通し（レンジと中心）は以下の通り。

日本国債１０年物利回り　２．８５―３．４５％（中心３．１５％）

日本国債３０年物利回り　３．８５―４．６５％（同４．２５％）

日本国債４０年物利回り　３．９５ ―４．７５％（同４．３５％）

米１０年債利回り　　　　４．３０─５．５０％（同４．９０％）

日経平均　　　　　　　 　６万４０００円─７万４０００円（同６万９０００円）

米ダウ　　　　　　　　　５万１０００─５万９０００ドル（同５万５０００ドル）

ドル／円　　　　　　　　１５２―１７２円（同１６２円）

ユーロ／円　　　　　　　１７３―１９８円（同１８８円）

item.title: ノルウェー政府系ファンド、株式・大手テック「やや慎重」 第3四半期は損失
item.description: ［オスロ ２２日 ロイター］ - 運用資産２兆３０００億ドルのノルウェー政府系ファンドは２２日、第３・四半期決算で２７...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ノルウェー政府系ファンド、株式・大手テック「やや慎重」　第3四半期は損失 13:40 配信

写真はノルウェー中央銀行の建物。2022年6月、オスロで撮影。REUTERS/Victoria Klesty

［オスロ　２２日　ロイター］ - 運用資産２兆３０００億ドルのノルウェー政府系ファンドは２２日、第３・四半期決算で２７８０億クローネ（２９７億ドル）の損失を計上したと発表するとともに、株式市場全体と一部の巨大ハイテク企業（ビッグテック）に対し「やや慎重」な姿勢を取ってきたと明らかにした。

同ファンドはノルウェー政府の石油・ガス生産による歳入を運用しており、世界の上場企業の平均１．５％を保有する世界最大の単独投資家となっている。

トロンド・グランデ副最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は決算発表後、ロイターに「公表してきた通り、われわれは株式市場全体についてやや慎重に、また大手ハイテク銘柄の一部についてもやや慎重に臨んできた」と述べ、「大局的に見れば、小幅なアンダーウエートにすぎない」と語った。

グランデ氏によると、ハイテク株の一部については「かなりの間」ややアンダーウエートとしており、現時点で変更する計画はないという。６月３０日時点でハイテクセクターはファンドの保有資産の２３％を占めている。

第３・四半期の世界での運用利回りはマイナス０．５％。金利上昇により、保有資産全体の２５．８％を占める債券ポートフォリオが打撃を受けたことが響いた。

item.title: Morning Bid: Wake up! The long bond's up two points!
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole. It's not every day you wake up to see the US long bond up 2 full points in price, but that's what happened overnight. Ten-year yields dived 19 basis points in the biggest daily move since early 2023, when Silicon Valley Bank collapsed. Fed funds futures rallied as much as 22 ticks, essentially taking an entire hike off the table for next year, while a December move is no longer fully priced in. Old-fashioned safe harbours were in demand as the yen and Swiss franc climbed, leaving the dollar looking a little less exceptional. The proximate cause this time was the sound of air escaping from the [USN:L6N4681D7 TEXT:"AI bubble"] as investors grappled with the sheer scale of funding needed for all this compute power. Some estimates put it at 1.6 times the cost of laying America's railways. Seems [USN:L6N468125 TEXT:"Meta's"] mention of needing "hundreds of billions of dollars" for capex [USN:L4N4681N3 TEXT:"spooked the horses"], with its shares sliding almost 7%. And not everyone was happy about the dilution from having to establish a whole new class of stock with no voting rights to raise the money. CoreWeave, the data center group that started much of this scare, shed another 10% of its value to hit lows last seen in May 2025, while credit spreads blew out across the entire sector. Treasuries benefited from the resulting scramble for safety, though that "safety" is relative these days. There is also the risk the investment boom in data centres will sputter, stalling a major driver of economic growth. Voter opposition to the energy-hungry sites has also been a notable feature of the midterm campaigns, adding politics to the mix. The surge in Treasuries might bring back memories of the Greenspan put, but it'll be much harder for the Fed to ride to the rescue this time. Brent futures are atop $113 a barrel, and over $100 right out to March, while crude for actual delivery is far higher. Easing monetary policy during an inflationary oil shock is going to be a hard sell. Neither is there any end in sight to the conflict in the Gulf. The press is full of reports of the White House considering fresh attacks on Iran after the midterms. The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group just departed Japan this week for Exercise Keen Sword 27, after which it will head for the Middle East. Ever since the war started in February, analysts have always assumed it would be done within a month or maybe two. Next week will mark the eighth month of the war, and it's not even clear whether Washington and Tehran are talking to each other. That will ensure inflation is front and centre when the Fed meets next week, relegating Wall Street's woes to a footnote. Key developments that could influence markets on Friday: - October global PMIs for Europe, UK and US. UK and Canada retail sales - Appearance by ECB board member Piero Cipollone (This story has been corrected to fix a typo in paragraph 5.)

item.title: マイクロソフト、医師のように「段階的に」診断するＡＩを開発
item.description:
Nancy Lapid
[２２日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトの研究者らは、医師のように段階を踏んで患者を診断する...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
マイクロソフト、医師のように「段階的に」診断するＡＩを開発 13:23 配信

マイクロソフトのロゴ。パリ近郊イシー・レ・ムリノーで25年3月撮影。REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes

Nancy Lapid

[２２日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトの研究者らは、医師のように段階を踏んで患者を診断する人工知能（ＡＩ）ツールが、複雑な症例の診断で一般診療医の２倍を超える正確さを示したと明らかにした。研究成果は２２日、科学誌サイエンスに掲載された。

報告によると、このモデルは、診断に協力して取り組む臨床専門家のチームを仮想的に再現し、ＡＩが問題に取り組む手順をまとめる「オーケストレーター」と呼ばれる仕組みを使い、患者に尋ねるべき質問や実施すべき診察・検査を特定し、調整する。

既存の医療ＡＩモデルは通常、患者の症状や臨床検査の結果、画像検査のデータを一括して分析し、診断を導き出す。

これに対し、このＡＩモデルではオーケストレーターが診断に至るまでの手順を調整する。まず、患者の病歴について何を尋ねるか、身体診察で何が重要かを判断する。得られた情報を基に実施する検査を決め、その結果を検討し、必要に応じて追加の検査を指示する。

研究責任者らはインタビューで、この過程を通じて、モデルは暫定的な仮説と診断計画を更新し続けると説明した。

極めてまれで診断が難しい３００件以上の症例を診断させたところ、診断オーケストレーターを用いたモデルは、教科書やインターネットを利用する一般診療医に比べ、患者の診察・検査を進めて診断を確定する正確さが２倍を超えた。

救急外来の受診記録を集めた大規模データベースに基づく症例でも、このツールは人間の医師を上回る成績を示した。

研究者らはまた、オーケストレーターが診察・検査の計画を立てた場合、人間の医師が計画した場合より診断にかかる費用が少ないことも確認した。

マイクロソフトＡＩヘルスのＡＩ責任者、ハーシャ・ノリ氏は「われわれはシステムの正確さだけを測っているのではない。どれだけ適切かつ慎重に診察・検査を進めるかも測っている」と述べた。

研究者らは今後、米ボストンのベス・イスラエル・ディーコネス医療センターと協力し、救急外来の待合室にいる患者の緊急度を判定して優先順位を決めるトリアージに、このツールを活用できるか検証する。

item.title: Gold steadies after three-month lows as oil rally fans inflation worries
item.description: Gold prices steadied after hitting a three-month low earlier on Friday but were on track for their steepest weekly loss since June, as rising oil prices fuelled higher-for-longer Federal Reserve rate expectations and pressured the non-yielding precious metal.
item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: Gold prices steadied after hitting a three-month low earlier on Friday but were on track for their steepest weekly loss since June, as rising oil prices fuelled higher-for-longer Federal Reserve rate expectations and pressured the non-yielding precious metal. Spot gold was at $4,023.95 per ounce by 1210 GMT after earlier dropping to $3,986.50, its lowest since July 20. Bullion has lost 3.5% so far this week, the second consecutive weekly loss. U.S. gold futures for December delivery fell 0.5% to $4,038.40 per ounce. "The rise in oil prices could result in real interest rates remaining higher for longer, which would reduce the relative attractiveness of investing in and holding gold," Hamad Hussain, climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics, said. Brent crude touched a more than five-month high on Friday, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies. Rising oil prices can stoke inflation, prompting investors to scale back Fed rate-cut bets. Last week's US [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer"] and [USN:L1N4610KT TEXT:"producer"] inflation data came in hotter than expected, largely because energy costs keep climbing. That strengthens the case for tighter policy, even though Fed officials are still expected to [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"hold off"] when they meet on October 27-28. Market expectations of a rate hike at the Fed's October 27–28 meeting are at 9%, while it is 81% for December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool . Investors are also awaiting US Personal Consumption Expenditures data, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, on October 29 for fresh clues on progress toward its 2% target. The [USN:L8N4651KP TEXT:"European Central Bank"] meets on Thursday against a backdrop of upheaval in France and an Iran war that is keeping energy prices above $100, meaning inflation risks remain elevated. Among other metals, spot silver slid 1.3% to $53.84 per ounce, and palladium dropped 0.6% to $1,047.69 per ounce, hitting their lowest since November 2025 and June 2025 respectively. Spot platinum edged down 0.8% to $1,558.18 per ounce, its lowest since July. All three metals were headed for weekly declines.

item.title: Trump says Bombardier to invest $270 million in the US
item.description: President Donald Trump said late on Thursday Canadian jet maker Bombardier was investing $270 million in the United States, days after he dropped threats to ban the company from the country.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said late on Thursday Canadian jet maker Bombardier (BBDb.TO) was investing $270 million in the United States, days after he [USN:L1N4660P1 TEXT:"dropped threats"] to ban the company from the country. Trump's September [USN:L1N44Z0HG TEXT:"threats against Bombardier"] became a political issue in Kansas, where it employs 1,500 people in Wichita. The threatened ban prompted calls to the White House from Kansas lawmakers, including Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who is facing a tough race in the November 3 elections. Bombardier will recruit for 500 roles across the US and is planning to create an extra 300 jobs through expansion projects, the company said in a statement on Friday. The expansion will include an initial investment of about $270 million for infrastructure growth in the first phase, per the statement. “Based on our constructive conversations with the U.S. administration, we see a bright path forward for our highly skilled aerospace workers as well as a positive environment for Bombardier to continue pursuing direct investments to grow our American footprint,” CEO Eric Martel said. The hiring will be spread across Texas, Kansas, Indiana and Connecticut, the company said. In a Truth Social post late on Thursday, Trump said Bombardier's investment would create thousands of jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana, and credited Marshall along with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton for the deal. Bombardier, which acquired Learjet and established its US headquarters in Kansas in 1990, has 3,500 jobs in the US, more than 40% of which are in Wichita. At a speech in Wichita on Monday, Trump said he did not plan to hurt Bombardier and would take care of its workers. "... now I find out they have a presence here, and we're not hurting them if they're in Kansas. So we'll take care of those people and the jobs," the president said in that speech. In February, Trump had threatened to decertify Bombardier aircraft over a certification dispute involving rival Gulfstream Aerospace. That threat never materialized because Transport Canada ultimately [USN:L1N3ZK0S8 TEXT:"approved the jets"].

item.title: 「金利に魅力」円債入れ替え加速、外債は残高維持に方針変更＝朝日生命・26年度下期運用計画
item.description:
Mayu Sakoda
[東京 ２３日 ロイター] - 朝日生命保険は２０２６年度下期の一般勘定資産運用で、国内債券に...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
「金利に魅力」円債入れ替え加速、外債は残高維持に方針変更＝朝日生命・26年度下期運用計画 13:08 配信

写真は円紙幣のイメージ。2022年11月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Mayu Sakoda

[東京 ２３日 ロイター] - 朝日生命保険は２０２６年度下期の一般勘定資産運用で、国内債券について高利回り銘柄への入れ替えを加速する方針を示した。金利が「魅力的な水準」に達したとして、超長期債を中心に買い入れる。外債は当初計画では圧縮を想定していたが、海外金利の上昇を受けて全体の残高は据え置きとする。

内村伸明資産運用企画部長が２０日、ロイターの取材で明らかにした。

円債運用では、金利水準が「ある程度の魅力的なところにきている」（内村氏）とみて短期債を売って長期・超長期債を買う入れ替えを上期より２倍程度、速いペースで行う。 将来の保険金支払いに備えて積み立てる責任準備金対応では、３０年債を中心に積み増す。

日銀の金融政策については、年度下期に２回の利上げを想定。財政悪化懸念が払拭されていないほか、利上げ継続で金利は一段と上昇する可能性もあるとみている。

外債運用については、年度計画の時点では円債への資金シフトに伴い残高の減少を見込んでいたが、海外金利も上昇していることから上期と同様に横ばいで維持する方針に変更した。低利回り債から高利回り債への乗り換えで、円債シフトと同等の利回り向上効果を実現できると判断した。

為替見通しでは、ドルは１５０円台の半ばから後半程度でのレンジ推移が続くと想定。デジタル赤字や対外直接投資など円安圧力となる要因は引き続き存在する一方で、大幅な円高進行のリスクは後退したとみている。ヘッジコストも依然として相応にかかることから、為替が現水準で安定している間はオープン比率を高めに維持する方針。

国内株式は、株高が進んだことで上期に一部を売却した。下期も底堅い企業業績などを背景に株高基調は続くとみており、売却で得た資金をオルタナティブ投資などに振り向ける。

不動産は中長期的に残高削減を続ける。

オルタナティブ投資は下期に１００億円積み増す計画で、インフラやプライベートエクイティなどを中心に投資する。プライベートクレジットを巡る信用懸念については保有資産への影響は出ておらず、投資案件の審査と分散投資でリスク管理を徹底する。

item.title: Ready for a French test?: Five questions for the ECB
item.description: The European Central Bank meets on Thursday against a backdrop of upheaval in France and an Iran war that is keeping energy prices above $100, meaning inflation risks remain elevated.
item.dc:creator: Dhara Ranasinghe, Stefano Rebaudo
item.content:encoded: The European Central Bank meets on Thursday against a backdrop of [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"upheaval in France"] and an Iran war that is keeping energy prices above $100, meaning inflation risks remain elevated. "How do you set rates against that backdrop? It's incredibly difficult," David Coombs, head of multi-asset investments at Rathbones Asset Management, said. Here's a look at five key questions for markets ahead of the October meeting. 1/ What will the ECB do? Leave its key interest rate unchanged at 2.5%. A pause is widely anticipated after the ECB raised rates in June and [USN:L1N452054 TEXT:"September"] to counter rising inflation, as the Iran war pushed up energy prices. Economists polled by Reuters [USN:L6N45T0G5 TEXT:"expect a quarter-point rate hike"] in December. "I don't think they've become materially less worried about inflation here," MUFG senior economist Henry Cook said. 2/ What will the ECB say about the rate outlook? It's likely to stick with a data-dependent approach. Caught between high inflation, at [USN:L8N45O0I3 TEXT:"3.8% in September"], and concerns that [USN:L1N45N082 TEXT:"rising government bond yields"] could hurt growth, policymakers have recently argued for what ECB President Christine Lagarde called a "[USN:L8N45K12P TEXT:"measured response"]." "There will be a definite flag to the tightening in financial conditions and how it should slow growth and hence curb inflationary pressures," said Barclays' head of euro rates strategy Rohan Khanna. "But also, plenty of uncertainty around the conflict and the outlook for energy prices." 3/ How worried is the ECB about an energy-driven inflation rise? Comments from officials such as ECB chief economist [USN:S8N3YE046 TEXT:"Philip Lane suggest"] the ECB is not overly worried, for now, about high energy costs leading to other prices and wages rising. A muted increase in core inflation, which excludes food and fuel prices, to [USN:L8N45O0I3 TEXT:"2.5% last month from 2.4%,"] suggests that high energy costs have yet to generate the sort of second-round impacts that could set off a hard-to-break inflation spiral. Still, with oil up almost 80% this year and headline inflation above its 2% target, the ECB will likely stress vigilance. "If the war in Iran escalates, or if we see further pressure on energy prices, the risk is still more rate hikes in 2027," said Bas van Geffen, senior macro strategist at Rabobank, adding he did not have any penciled in for next year. Markets price in at least two hikes by mid-2027. 4/ What about the French bond selloff? Well, the ECB is watching. French 10-year borrowing costs just hit [USN:L8N4670MT TEXT:"24-year highs above 5%"] and a weakened government is grappling with violent protests that could undermine efforts to improve fragile finances. Also, the premium investors demand to hold 10-year French bonds over safer Germany is at 170 bps, up from 92 bps when the ECB met last month. But don't expect the ECB to act soon with measures such as the [USN:L1N45N0CH TEXT:"Transmission Protection Instrument"] that allows it to buy bonds from any member state experiencing an "unwarranted, disorderly" tightening of its financing conditions. France should [USN:L1N46002V TEXT:"solve its own debt problems"] through fiscal consolidation, says Lagarde. The ECB could hold back on rate hikes if it thinks a crisis in France could hurt economic growth materially, Berenberg chief economist Holger Schmieding said. "If there are serious contagion effects from a hypothetical French crisis to other countries where the fiscal policy is much more sustainable, the ECB would probably use its TPI to shield these other countries, not France," he said. 5/ Who will replace Lagarde? The ECB chief, who could be appointed as the [USN:L6N4610XU TEXT:"next World Economic Forum chair"] as early as November, will likely be pressed on succession. The former central bank governors of the Netherlands and Spain, [USN:FWN45G19M TEXT:"Klaas Knot"] and Pablo Hernandez de Cos, are seen as frontrunners. Lagarde's exit would open a second vacancy on the ECB's six-member Executive Board after [USN:L6N45V0R7 TEXT:"Isabel Schnabel's recent resignation"]. Chief economist Lane is meanwhile due to step down in May. Lagarde's term is scheduled to end next October. Leaving early allows time for a new ECB chief to be picked before France's spring presidential election. A snap Spanish election could also impact the [USN:L8N46305T TEXT:"politics around ECB succession"], analysts said.

item.title: 午前のドルは156円後半に持ち直し、仲値後に実需の買い観測も
item.description:
Noriyuki Hirata

午前のドルは156円後半に持ち直し、仲値後に実需の買い観測も 12:36 配信

米ドル紙幣。8月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Noriyuki Hirata

[東京 ２３日 ロイター] - 午前のドルは朝方に軟化した後、１５６円後半に持ち直した。全国消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）の２％超えや日経平均の下落を嫌気した売りが先行し、一時１５６円前半に下落した。その後は株価が下げ渋る中でショートカバーが入ったほか、仲値後に実需の買いが入ったとの観測もあって一時１５７円を回復した。

・日経平均の下落を眺めてドルは一時１５６．０８円に下落

・米金利低下によるドル売りやＣＰＩの結果を受けた円買いも意識

・実質的に実需筋の取引が集中しやすい五・十日

・仲値にかけて株価が下げ渋り、ドル／円にはショートカバーも

・仲値後は急速に持ち直す動きになり、一時１５７円前半を回復

・ショートカバーに加え、まとまった実需の買いが入ったとの観測も

・ＡＩ株安や仏財政悪化への警戒感はくすぶる

＜三菱ＵＦＪ信託銀行 資金為替部上級調査役 岡田佑介氏＞

「この１━２日の動きはポジション調整の範囲内だろう」

「円キャリーを背景にした円売り需要は変わっておらず、ドルは押し目を拾いたい人は多い」

「米中間選挙での（民主党勝利を受けた）米ＡＩ株売り、ドル売りを意識する向きも出始めたか」

item.title: Apple's iPhone Duo hits stores in face of short supply, high demand
item.description: The iPhone lineup is Apple’s largest moneymaker, generating roughly half of the company’s revenue. And the Duo is the biggest single design change in the device’s nearly two-decade history. Though the ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Mark Gurman Apple Inc. has already shown there’s a strong appetite for its $2,000-and-up foldable iPhone Duo. Now it needs to meet that demand. The new device goes on sale Friday, with the first shipments reaching Apple retail stores around the world. It also will begin arriving at the homes of customers who ordered quickly enough to secure day-one deliveries. The launch is bringing back a once-familiar sight: lines outside Apple stores. Such crowds have largely disappeared in recent years after Apple, retailers like Best Buy Co. and wireless carriers began maintaining enough inventory to fulfill most orders through home delivery or appointment-based store pickups. This time is different. Supplies for preorders were so limited that many customers hoping to get the Duo on launch day have little choice but to line up and see whether their local store has any inventory available. Apple is allocating a small portion of its stock for those people.  At the company’s flagship Fifth Avenue store in New York City, where top Apple executives typically open the doors to buyers, there was a line of customers without preorders that reached more than a few dozen people by the early evening on Thursday. There were similar lines in Asia and Australia. As one of the most expensive mainstream smartphones ever sold, the Duo had raised questions about just how much demand there would be. But early adopters, resellers and everyday Apple fans have demonstrated that the interest is there. The iPhone lineup is Apple’s largest moneymaker, generating roughly half of the company’s revenue. And the Duo is the biggest single design change in the device’s nearly two-decade history. Though the company wasn’t first to market with a foldable phone, it looks to gain an edge with a more polished product built for Apple fans. Rather than a repeat of the lackluster debut of the Vision Pro headset nearly three years ago, the Duo’s launch is shaping up to be a throwback to the iPhone introductions of old — when demand far outstripped supply. That’s the case even with device prices reaching as high as $3,199 for models with 2 terabytes of storage. Though the Duo’s cost sets a record for a mass-market smartphone, Apple’s competitors such as Samsung Electronics Co. have been raising prices as well. Shortages of memory chips and other components have made consumer electronics more expensive across the board.  Consumers placing new orders for the Duo on Apple’s website are now being offered delivery at the end of January, though some early buyers have seen their January shipping estimates move up to as soon as November or December. The delays mark some of the lengthiest for a new Apple product in the company’s modern era. The phones are difficult to produce because of their advanced hinge and new display technology. They’re also only built in a limited number of facilities in China. Apple expanded production in recent years for its traditional iPhones, including to India, which has helped with supply.  Apple reports its quarterly earnings results on Nov. 2, but the period won’t include sales of the Duo because the period concluded around the end of September. It will reflect early sales of iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models, which debuted on Sept. 18. Other new versions, such as the entry-level iPhone or the updated Air, won’t go on sale until next year, Bloomberg News has reported. That marks a change in the company’s usual release schedule, a move meant to help spread out revenue across the year.

item.description: [東京 ２３日 ロイター] - 日本製鉄は２３日、傘下の米鉄鋼大手ＵＳスチールが運営する米ペンシルベニア州モンバレ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
日鉄、ＵＳスチールの製鉄所に約30億ドル投資　熱延設備刷新 12:29 配信

日鉄のロゴ。東京都内で24年4月撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

[東京　２３日　ロイター] - 日本製鉄は２３日、傘下の米鉄鋼大手ＵＳスチールが運営する米ペンシルベニア州モンバレー製鉄所に新たな熱延設備を建設すると発表した。約３０億ドルを投じる。

今回の投資は、同社が２０２５年のＵＳスチール買収に伴い、２８年までに総額１１０億ドルを投資するとしていた計画の具体化の１つ。

既存設備を新鋭設備に更新することで年間生産能力を現在の約２２０万トンから約３５０万トンに拡大する。許認可取得後に建設を開始し、２９年後半の稼働開始を予定している。

item.title: Oil spill off UAE coast prompts beach closures, cleanup effort
item.description: The United Arab Emirates said efforts were under way on Friday to contain oil leaking from a tanker vessel offshore that prompted authorities to close beaches and warn fishermen to avoid the area.
item.dc:creator: Maha Dahan, Sarah Safty
item.content:encoded: The United Arab Emirates said efforts were under way on Friday to contain oil leaking from a tanker vessel offshore that prompted authorities to close beaches and warn fishermen to avoid the area. Since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran , attacks on commercial vessels in Gulf shipping lanes have driven up security risks for maritime traffic and heightened fears over the conflict's environmental fallout. The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said in a statement that containment operations had been launched and an environmental assessment was being carried out. All beaches and coastal areas around the city of Umm Al Quwain had been temporarily closed until technical teams completed their assessments and determined the necessary safety and marine protection measures, it said. The ministry also urged fishermen and other sea users to avoid affected areas and follow official instructions. ANALYST IDENTIFIES LEAKING TANKER AS THE GEM NO.2 UAE authorities have not named the tanker involved in the incident or said what caused the spill. And the environment ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. However, Martin Kelly, CEO of Orbital Risk Intelligence, told Reuters that the spill was coming from a tanker called the Gem No.2. Shipping sources said on October 9 that the Gem No.2 was [USN:L1N45V0GU TEXT:"struck"] by an unidentified projectile 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera in the UAE, causing a fire that was later extinguished. While no group claimed responsibility, maritime security sources told Reuters at the time that the incident occurred outside the Strait of Hormuz and pointed to a widening of risks for commercial shipping. Earlier that week, a tanker was also struck off the coast of Qatar inside the Gulf. SPILL PUTTING COASTAL INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK Maritime intelligence firm Windward first identified the spill on Tuesday, writing in a post on X that a VLCC-sized vessel was leaking oil about 25 km (16 miles) off Umm Al Quwain. Prevailing currents, it said at the time, could carry the slick southwest toward the UAE coastline. "Windward's drift model shows it reaching Sharjah's and Ajman's desalination intakes and ports by (October 22–23) if the leak isn't stopped," it wrote on X. The UAE relies on desalination plants for most of its drinking water, and much of the economy — including ports and industrial facilities — is also located on the coast, making any contamination along its shoreline particularly sensitive. Residents in some areas had posted on social media about strange odours. The ministry, however, said that odours reported in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain posed no health risks. The spill follows a [USN:L8N4490KK TEXT:"separate"] tanker-related environmental incident in August, when oil from a tanker that ran aground off Oman began reaching the mainland coast.

item.title: Data centres fail as AI pick-and-shovel trade
item.description: NextDC shares fell 42% after community backlash delayed power upgrades at one site. Investors are wising up to the trade-offs of massive debt-financed spending, slow-moving utilities, chip shortages and impatient hyperscaler clients like OpenAI with ironclad get-out clauses.
item.dc:creator: Antony Currie
item.content:encoded: So much for a safe bet on the AI revolution. The smart advice for investing in potential bubbles is to find the modern equivalent of the picks and shovels of the US gold rush in the 1800s. For today's artificial intelligence trade, data centre providers were supposed to be one of them: no matter whether hyperscalers like OpenAI and Anthropic or any of the other developers of software succeed or fail, the demand for places to host the hardware needed is too strong to shatter. But the stock price crashes at Australia's NextDC (NXT.AX) and its US neocloud rival CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , and the [USN:L6N45V00W TEXT:"aborted $5.5 billion IPO"] of Firmus Technologies, confirm that investors are realising it's not that simple. Start with the non-financial problems. Data centre developers want to build as fast as possible to meet their hyperscaler clients' voracious demand for compute and inference capacity. Trouble is, that can lead to high expectations, poor planning and dismal community relations, even for players like NextDC, whose shares fell 42% on Wednesday, that have been in operation for decades. Semiconductor shortages continue, for example. And utilities need more than a few months to get water and electricity hooked up - one water provider told Breakingviews conversations ought to start up to three years before developers buy the land. Nscale in the UK [USN:L6N4650TB TEXT:"lost a contract"] with Microsoft (MSFT.O) after being told power would not be available until 2030. NextDC similarly misread local opposition to its M3 site in Melbourne right across the street from a residential neighbourhood: the resulting delays to installing up to 22-metre-high concrete poles to carry 66,000-volt cables forced CEO Craig Scroggie to slash its EBITDA forecast by a third, cease projects with no contracts and consider selling undeveloped sites. Such issues can then cascade. Constructing data centres requires lots of investment. That's mostly done with debt, usually raised only once a contract has been signed. While that sounds smart, it leaves the borrower at the mercy of iron-clad get-out clauses. One is the availability clause: if water or power connections are delayed by a stipulated timeframe, if a natural disaster strikes or if chips are either unavailable or subpar, then the hyperscaler client can walk. There's also a more general delay clause, which usually stipulates the customer can cancel the entire contract if completion of the data centre is more than 12 months late. It's bad news for traditional data centre builders and neoclouds alike. They could be left with the unenviable mix of part-finished projects, unused land, underwhelming or no earnings and heaps of debt. Hardly a picks-and-shovels trade. Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn . Shares in NextDC closed down 42% on October 21 after the Australian data centre builder and operator cut its underlying EBITDA forecast for the financial year to the end of June by more than a third. The company now expects EBITDA of A$245 million to A$265 million ($172 million to $186 million) for the period. CEO Craig Scroggie also said he is putting on hold all projects not already backed by customer contracts, has started a "detailed review" of the company's capital expenditure programme and is open to selling development sites that "are not required in the near term". The move came after Jemena Electricity Networks informed NextDC that it has suspended some of the work to increase power supply to its M3 data centre in Melbourne following "community and stakeholder opposition". Last month local residents used their vehicles and other methods to prevent Jemena from installing concrete electricity poles of up to 22-metres in height that are needed to carry the 66,000-volt power lines the data centre will require. Scroggie also noted that the company had some A$8.7 billion of liquidity at the end of September. Meanwhile, on October 20, after local opposition Amazon abandoned plans to build four data centres on a site it had bought from George Washington University in Virginia in the US. The company also agreed to donate $5 million to the county's housing trust fund. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Brent crude hits more than five-month high on concern over Middle East escalation
item.description: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Kelly
item.content:encoded: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures gained $1.40, or 1.2%, to $114.57 a barrel by 1138 GMT, having earlier reached $115 for the highest level since May 4. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $1.48, or 1.5%, to $100.95. The Brent benchmark is on track for a third consecutive weekly gain, of 4.2%, while WTI is poised to finish 0.5% down on the week. Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) on Thursday [USN:L1N46809Q TEXT:"ordered the evacuation"] of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters reported, as fighting intensified between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis. "The market remains concerned about a potential escalation, which, in a worst-case scenario, could trigger renewed supply disruptions," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that volatile oil flows and elevated freight rates have left the market undersupplied. Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognised government have raged since the Iran-aligned Houthis pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea. "The key factors to monitor now are the extent of actual disruption and the time needed to restore operations, as these will ultimately determine how much of a supply risk premium the market is willing to pay," said XS.com analyst Linh Tran. "If attacks persist and delay deliveries, elevated prices will have a firmer foundation." An oil spill from a tanker [USN:L1N469029 TEXT:"was detected"] off the coast of Umm Al Quwain, prompting containment operations and environmental assessments, the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said on Friday. The ministry did not say what caused the spill and authorities have not identified the tanker involved. In Libya, an oil pipeline valve from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port has been shut, leading to a reduction in production at both fields, the head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday. Meanwhile, the first Russian diesel [USN:L1N4690EB TEXT:"bound for the US"] since a surprise agreement between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed on Friday. Trump announced the [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal"] this month as part of his efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of US midterm elections next month.

SEOUL, Oct 23 : HD Hyundai Co said on Friday it has signed a deal with Kiewit Corp to start building an advanced US shipyard next year, with operations expected to begin in 2029 and create about 3,000 domestic jobs. The new shipyard is expected to boost US shipbuilding capacity and help revive the industry, Hyundai said. The partners will explore opportunities in both commercial ships and military support vessels, it said in a statement.  • South Korea pledged to invest $150 billion in the US shipbuilding sector, as part of $350 billion of investment funds the Asian country agreed to put into US projects in return for winning U.S. tariff cuts in last year. • Construction of the shipyard will begin in 2027 and the two companies will also set up a joint venture. • The joint venture will explore building US navy support vessels, commercial ship opportunities, and supplying ship blocks and modules to US shipyards. • HD Hyundai said the new shipyard is expected to revive the US shipbuilding industry and expand Korea-US shipbuilding cooperation.

Source: Reuters

item.title: US corporate profit boom faces its ‘Minsky moment’
item.description: Earnings for the S&P 500 Index rose 26% in the past year. Tech giants and chipmakers at the heart of the AI boom make up more than half the surge. Depreciation delays and investments in unlisted firms inflate bottom lines. As the economist Hyman Minsky wrote, it cannot last.
item.dc:creator: Edward Chancellor
item.content:encoded: The artificial intelligence generated by large language models is breathtaking. Equally wonderous is the financial alchemy that accompanies multi-trillion-dollar investments in AI infrastructure. Capital spending is instantaneously transformed into profits, even as the economic viability of the AI buildout remains questionable. The United States is in the throes of a great profit boom. Corporate profits had reached a record $4.7 trillion for the last twelve months by mid-year. That’s a 17% increase on the previous year’s figures. Tax breaks contained in President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act have led to a sharp drop in corporate tax receipts. Washington’s enormous fiscal deficit – running at around 6% of GDP – provides an economy wide fillip to corporate bottom lines. When it comes to individual companies, however, the surge is all about AI. Earnings per share for members of the S&P 500 Index (.SPX) were up 26% in the twelve months to July: the long-run average annual growth rate is 7%. Expected earnings for the third quarter are 35% above estimates from a year ago. Gerard Minack of Minack Advisors lists 19 members of the S&P 500 that are heavily involved in the AI buildout: Big Tech “hyperscalers”, chipmakers and supply-chain companies such as fibre-optic provider Corning (GLW.N) . Since January 2025, these “AI-19 stocks” have seen forecast earnings rise by around $700 billion, 50% more than all the other companies in the US stock market benchmark. Analysts at Morgan Stanley predict that 42 leading companies exposed to AI will grow their earnings by 67% in 2026. The aggregate earnings growth of the other S&P 500 companies is projected at 23%. Put another way, these 42 stocks account for more than half of the earnings growth for the S&P 500 in the current year. Next year Morgan Stanley expects the basket of AI plays to contribute 78% of the S&P 500 earnings growth as AI investment in the United States rises to a forecast $1.6 trillion. “This is the probably the most earnings accretive capex boom in history,” says Jefferies strategist Christopher Wood. AI capital spending inflates profits because, as Minack points out, one company’s capex is another’s revenue. Profits emerge because the investing company does not expense all its costs at once, whereas the seller of capital equipment immediately books the full amount as revenue. Buyers of Nvidia’s (NVDA.O) graphics processing units depreciate their purchases on average over around 6 years, while the chip giant books a juicy upfront profit. What’s more, when the buyer is acquiring chips for a data centre that is under construction, the depreciation clock does not start ticking until the facility is up and running. Morgan Stanley estimates that as much as 40% of this year’s AI capex will become operational sometime between 2027 and 2029. The earnings mirage will not last indefinitely, though. By the end of the decade, the hyperscalers’ annual depreciation charges will range between $500 billion and $1 trillion, according to a recent report from Capital Gearing Asset Management. Investments in unlisted AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are also super-charging profits. Tech giants reflect changes in the private market value of these investments in their earnings statements as “other non-operating income.” In the four quarters leading up to mid-2026, the four major hyperscalers – Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , and Meta Platforms (META.O) – saw annualized earnings increase by $222 billion while "other non-operating income" rose by $224 billion. In other words, the rising value of unlisted AI investments accounted for all the increase in their reported earnings. The fact that the AI buildout is increasingly financed with debt adds a further element of instability. The hyperscalers will plough almost all their operating cash flow into capex in the current financial year. These companies have issued around $225 billion of unsecured bonds so far this year, equivalent to around 30% of their full-year capital spending. They also have lease commitments for $1.1 trillion of AI equipment and services, which, since they haven’t yet commenced, are not reported on their balance sheets. Next year, Morgan Stanley analysts forecast the hyperscalers will have negative free cash flow of around $550 billion. “Access to credit markets and the ability to absorb higher interest rates are fundamental for hyperscalers and neoclouds to be able to deliver against our capex estimates,” says the Wall Street bank. That shouldn’t be too much of a problem for giants like Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta which enjoy solid credit ratings because of their dominant positions in search, software, online retailing and social media. The economist Hyman Minsky applied the term “Ponzi finance” to businesses that do not generate sufficient cash flows to meet their outgoings. Loss-making data centre operators and AI frontier labs fit this description. Ponzi finance units, said Minsky, need rising valuations to raise additional capital. When valuations decline and the capital markets seize up, these shaky institutions collapse, causing losses to metastasise through the financial system. That is what happened in early 2000 after the credit markets lost confidence in the debt-fuelled buildout of the information superhighway. That investors are starting to question the viability of the AI investment splurge should come as no surprise. Productivity improvements from implementing the new technology remain elusive. Rogue AI agents are causing havoc. Models continue to hallucinate. Chinese AI companies are rapidly taking market share from the leading US AI labs. OpenAI has pushed back its planned IPO while upstart data centre operators such as [USN:L6N45V00W TEXT:"Firmus Technologies"] have shelved their stock offerings. Prospective investors in Anthropic are [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"weighing a lower valuation"] for the AI company, Reuters reported citing four people familiar with the matter. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , the largest neocloud, has seen its [USN:L6N46113K TEXT:"shares and bonds tumble"]. The shares of hyperscalers and chipmakers do not look expensive relative to earnings. That’s because the bubble is in profits, not valuations. US homebuilders were in the same position at the peak of the housing bubble in 2006, as were global miners when the commodity supercycle came to a sudden stop in the middle of the last decade. When the AI capex boom ends, earnings growth could revert to trend, says Minack. That moment may come sooner rather than later. Follow @Breakingviews on X

FAST

NEW YORK: US stocks tumbled on Thursday (Oct 22) and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race. The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq , dragged down by microchips, suffered a steeper loss, falling 2.6 per cent in the wake of a spate of high-profile AI-related earnings results. The blue-chip Dow eked out a nominal gain minutes before the closing bell. Meta Platforms' results beat analyst expectations, but its stock slid 7.0 per cent as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the nascent technology.

Tesla shares fell 3.1 per cent even though the electric car maker unexpectedly posted positive free cash flow in the quarter and cut its 2026 capital spending plans. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index .SOX , which has driven much of the current bull market's gains, plunged 6.7 per cent , its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23. With Thursday's decline, the SOX is off more than 26 per cent from its record closing high reached on Jun 22, yet it remains up 51.5 per cent so far this year. The S&P 500 has risen 11.9 per cent over the same period. "It's a wonderful day on Wall Street," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser & market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "The only part of the market that is really suffering here is technology, which has been the golden child of the markets up until about June." "Investors are starting to realize that there are some holes in the AI story," Nolte added. "And that's having an impact on the indices because they're so heavily weighted toward technology." On the geopolitical stage, Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi targets, sending crude prices to a five-month high. Investors worried that ongoing Middle East strife could keep inflation hot and force the US Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates. Data from the Labour Department showed initial claims for unemployment benefits kept drifting along near multi-decade lows. Signs of labor market stability will allow the Fed to focus on fighting inflation. Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end. The Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI rose 11.89 points, or 0.02 per cent, to 52,867.98, the S&P 500 .SPX lost 93.74 points, or 1.21 per cent, to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC lost 694.00 points, or 2.60 per cent, to 26,008.86.

Related:

Commentary: Every investment portfolio looks like the same trade - AI

Third-quarter earnings season is well underway, with 111 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 83 per cent have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data. Procter & Gamble warned that rising cost pressures would take an increasing bite out of profit, but beat analyst estimates, sending the stock 5.6 per cent higher and supporting consumer staples .SPLRCS . Blackstone advanced 8.4 per cent , after the company said widening credit spreads on AI-related debt could present an opportunity to lock in higher returns. Lockheed Martin climbed 7.0 per cent after the aerospace/defense firm raised its annual sales and profit forecast. Spotify rose 11.1 per cent after the Swedish music streaming firm forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, betting on its AI-powered features to drive user growth. Union Pacific gained 3.6 per cent following the company's quarterly earnings beat, which was helped by core pricing gains, although the railroad flagged a hit from rising fuel prices. Chipmakers Intel, AMD, Sandisk and Marvell all tumbled more than 8 per cent amid the broader semiconductor selloff. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.01-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 173 new highs and 366 new lows on the NYSE. On the Nasdaq , 2,022 stocks rose and 2,766 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.37-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 40 new 52-week highs and four new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 82 new highs and 342 new lows. Volume on US exchanges was 18.79 billion shares, compared with the 17.19 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

item.title: Apple's foldable iPhone hits stores with $2,000 price tag and scarce supply
item.description: Apple's first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, hit stores around the world on Friday with a price tag of about $2,000 and less of the fanfare that accompanied previous iPhone launches.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni, Christine Chen, Will Russell
item.content:encoded: Apple's (AAPL.O) first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, hit stores around the world on Friday with a price tag of about $2,000 and less of the fanfare that accompanied previous iPhone launches. From Singapore and Shanghai to London and Berlin, demand was strong but with sales rationed, there were fewer of the round-the-block queues and overnight camp-outs that once marked new iPhone days. Competitors such as Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and Huawei Technologies have sold premium foldable phones for years and the Duo is a test of whether Apple can reinvent the small foldable mobile market the way the iPhone did for smartphones. It is also an early challenge for Apple's new CEO John Ternus, the former hardware chief who unveiled the phone barely a week after taking charge in September. Apple's estimated delivery dates for the Duo had slipped to late January within minutes of pre-orders opening a week ago, as demand outpaced supply. The US company called the response "nothing short of extraordinary". Apple capped pre-orders at two handsets per customer and limited sales to walk-in shoppers. In China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan they were only available to those who had ordered online. In Sydney, which was the first Apple store to sell the new passport-shaped phones on Friday, a queue formed outside before opening at 8 a.m. local time (2100 GMT). "This is a bit of a luxury item for me, because it's so expensive, but I just think, you know what? Life's too short," said Simon Krishnan, a 48-year-old engineer who paid A$3,899 ($2,734) for a 512GB Duo. In China, a soft consumer market and rising memory costs have led to [USN:P8N44H02N TEXT:"six straight quarters"] of declining smartphone shipments, although Apple's market share has rebounded as some buyers trade up to premium devices. Liu Wei, a 26-year-old healthcare professional, already has a foldable phone from Xiaomi (1810.HK) , but still queued outside a Shanghai store from 6 a.m. for Apple's first foldable. "I've used Apple products for many years and I have more trust (in the brand), so I bought one on launch day to try it out," he said. Many queued to pick up pre-orders, while others hoped for limited stock or to browse display models. Others were resellers. In Hong Kong, May, 38, who declined to give his full name, bought a 256GB iPhone Duo, priced at HK$17,499 ($2,231.73), in an online pre-sale and planned to resell it for a profit of around HK$4,000. "A few meals' worth of money," he joked. Paul Francis, 53, was one of several dozen fans who queued overnight outside London's Regent Street store in pouring rain. "Some people think it was mad. Including myself," the charity manager said. MIXED REVIEWS Early reviews have praised the Duo's design as well as its sturdy and barely visible hinge, a major feat for phones whose prominent creased screen has long been a drawback and potential deterrent for buyers. But reviewers said camera compromises, including no telephoto lens, and third-party apps still to be reworked for the new display size could disappoint some buyers. They also said the folded Duo is less handy for the quick tasks most users do daily and several prominent reviewers recommended against it for many Apple customers. "It's been a lot of fun trying the Duo out for a week, but it feels like I've gotten to use an extraordinarily polished prototype — not a finished product that I'd want to buy and carry," wrote longtime Apple commentator John Gruber. Tech commentator Marques Brownlee said in a YouTube review that for a regular person who mostly texts and browses, "it is probably a no. But if the $2,000 doesn't mean much to you, and you like the idea, after the learning curve and getting used to not having facial identification, it is a really fun phone." In Berlin, YouTube content creator Patrick Wolter was impressed that the Duo works as a phone and an iPad in one. "I've always found it a hassle to carry around a separate tablet, especially since I already have a laptop and other gear," he said. "In the long run, this will likely end up replacing those other devices." TOUGH TO FIND Apple's entry into the relatively niche foldables market could bring the format to a much broader audience, said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president at market researcher IDC. IDC expects Apple will take 44% of the foldable market value in 2026 on 31% of units. By 2027, it will become the market leader both in value and units shipped, IDC forecast. "Apple has made a convincing case for this form factor," Jeronimo said after spending a week with the Duo. "Now comes the next test: turning excitement into availability, adoption and a lasting new chapter for the smartphone market," Jeronimo said. ($1 = 1.4257 Australian dollars) ($1 = 7.8410 Hong Kong dollars)

item.title: Trump says Musk restored Ukraine's Starlink access, declines to say if they spoke
item.description: Ukraine uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage , Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump said on Thursday that SpaceX (SPCX.O) CEO Elon Musk had restored Ukraine's Starlink access but the US president declined to comment when asked whether he had spoken to the billionaire about the matter. The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Thursday that Trump had called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starlink. "I don't want to comment on it, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn't make any difference, I guess. The bottom line - he put it back," Trump told reporters when asked if he spoke to Musk. Trump did not elaborate further. Ukraine uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations. Restricting the satellite service [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"hampered"] the country's attack and air defense drone missions against Russia. The Starlink system was working more normally on Thursday, shortly after the Trump-Musk conversation, the WSJ reported earlier, citing US and Ukrainian officials. Some Ukrainian officials told the newspaper the system had not been restored to full functionality but was working at higher speeds than under the cap. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said earlier on Thursday that speed on Starlink systems had not been restored for Ukraine, adding that he hoped for talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in the coming days. Trump told Musk he was frustrated the system's speeds remained capped, according to the newspaper. Trump has denied being involved in the decision concerning the slowdown. Rubio told reporters on Wednesday that decisions regarding Ukraine's [USN:L6N467096 TEXT:"access to Starlink"] were up to its parent company SpaceX and Musk, not the White House. Zelenskiy's relations with Washington have sunk to new lows after Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and waived new sanctions on Moscow. Trump has also told Kyiv to stop attacking Russian refineries and urged Ukrainians to replace Zelenskiy. Russia [USN:L1N4671BN TEXT:"pounded Kyiv"] with ballistic missiles and Ukraine sent hundreds of drones towards Moscow on Thursday, as the warring sides kept up a barrage of attacks despite the latest US push to end the conflict. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022. Trump had promised to end the war when he took office but the goal has remained elusive.

item.title: Steep bill for AI buildout punishes Meta, other tech favorites
item.description: The tab for the next round of the AI buildout came due on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Lewis Krauskopf, Sudeshna Ghoshal
item.content:encoded: The tab for the next round of the AI buildout came due on Thursday. Investors sold shares of Meta Platforms (META.O) and a wealth of companies central to the AI trade, a day after Meta — one of the hyperscalers spending billions to build data centers and other infrastructure supporting the AI boom — said it would issue a new class of shares that will help it raise funds. Meta fell 7%, its largest drop since July. SpaceX (SPCX.O) declined 9% and semiconductor company Nvidia (NVDA.O) — a bellwether of the AI trade — dropped 4%. The Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 2.6%, its largest decline since June 5. Sentiment was also hurt by a 12% plunge in shares of semiconductor company Lam Research (LRCX.O) following its results. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index (.SOX) lost 6.7%. The pullback is the latest test for the AI trade as investors focus on the rising costs of long-term projects where the payoff remains uncertain. Tech firms have borrowed huge sums over the past year for AI spending, but Wall Street now expects that the rise in borrowing costs will motivate tech companies like Meta to sell billions of dollars in stock to fund the next round of building. That dilution could put pressure on share prices, and is a potentially unwelcome development when major US stock indexes remain near all-time highs despite a punishing month of volatile trading. RETURN ON INVESTMENT CONCERNS Selling started with "the big question about the (return on investment) on all the spending," said Matthew Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak. "It's just becoming more and more evident to people that it's going to take a lot longer." Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital LLC in New York, agreed that ROI concerns are central while also citing remarks by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about a financing bottleneck for smaller AI companies as contributing to the selling. Meta said on Wednesday it would use new Class C shares, which hold no voting power, to [USN:l4n4671s3 TEXT:"fund AI spending and other priorities"]. Meta also raised the low end of its annual spending forecast to $135 billion from $130 billion, with the high end unchanged at $145 billion. That level of spending will require lots of investor participation in coming stock sales. Meta reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, compared with positive free cash flow of $10.63 billion a year earlier. It was the first cash burn at Meta in more than a decade. “More spending, negative free cash flow, not enough revenue being generated from the spend (is) concerning investors that this is just sort of a bit of a money pit,” said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield, Connecticut. The action highlights concern over how AI investment will be paid for. Credit default swaps, which track perceived default risk for the debt of the biggest AI players, have largely risen over the past year, with Meta’s hitting a record on Thursday . INVESTOR ANXIETY SHOWS Fresh signs of market anxiety over AI spending snowballed into a broad market selloff Thursday, with some saying an AI pullback could hit US growth. Investors sought the safety of Treasury bonds, sending those prices higher . "This is your classic rotation day,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner, co-founder and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey. “You can see the money going into Treasuries, so it's a classic safety move ... They are rotating out of techs, out of the AIs, and into the more safety trades, whether it's bonds or some of those big Dow Jones stocks.” Thursday’s selloff added to the pressure on the neocloud companies at the heart of the AI buildout, with Nebius (NBIS.O) off 7% after announcing a new $3.5 billion credit line from Citigroup and CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , whose unsecured bond yields soared to 15% in last week’s AI selloff, down 10%. Bank of America analyst Tal Liani said in a report on Thursday he is maintaining a buy rating and a price target of $140 on CoreWeave stock heading into next month’s earnings report, though he said he believes the firm will need to raise $20 billion to fund commitments to customers — the sort of prospect that is generating anxiety among tech investors. "Nobody is worried about Meta or Amazon or Google getting the financing they need," Maley said. "But if it gets prohibitive for smaller companies, then you don't have to have an implosion of things to make people nervous."

US President Donald Trump criticised NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday (Oct 23) for what he called disrespectful behaviour during the singing of the national anthem at a recent NBA game. "While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country," Trump said in a Truth Social post accompanied by a video showing James moving his body during the singing of the anthem. "LeBron James should apologise to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!" The clip Trump shared showed James standing in line with the members of the Philadelphia 76ers, swinging his arms in a warmup-type stretch and performing basketball shooting movements. A representative for the 76ers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump has repeatedly criticised athletes for their behaviour during pre-game renditions of the US national anthem, notably beginning with NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick's kneeling protest in support of racial justice. Trump cancelled a planned White House visit of the Super Bowl champions Philadelphia Eagles in 2018 after the team disagreed with his call for players to stand during the anthem. James became a leading voice in the Black Lives Matter movement in 2020 and has frequently supported progressive issues as he ascended to the top of the NBA's all-time scoring list.

item.title: Blackstone sets up $10 bln test of banks’ AI risk
item.description: The buyout shop and co-owner Warburg Pincus want to sell IntraFi, which lets lenders offer deposit insurance beyond a statutory $250,000 cap. The mooted value represents 400% growth over seven years. It’s just awkward timing as fears rise of autonomous agents managing balances.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Gandel
item.content:encoded: Private equity is about to find out whether bankers should really be worried. Digital assistants like Meta’s (META.O) Muse threaten to upend lenders' businesses: if artificial intelligence can automatically move deposits to high-interest accounts, cheap balances might disappear. They could also theoretically mimic IntraFi, a company built entirely on cash-shuffling. Buyout shops Blackstone (BX.N) and Warburg Pincus want to offload the so-called reciprocal deposit network for $10 billion, [USN:L6N4651A1 TEXT:"Reuters reported"] on Tuesday. Such a big return could somewhat allay technological fears. IntraFi is not a bank, yet it [USN:L6N45N19E TEXT:"benefits from the same frictions"] that protect lenders’ deposit franchises. Thanks to consumer inertia, large banks get away with paying little or no interest on many accounts, which provides cheap funding to issue loans at far higher yields. Executives like JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon have brushed off concerns that so-called agents like Muse could automate away this cozy equilibrium. The new sale process offers a kind of test on how investors feel. Deposit juggling is IntraFi’s specialty. Depositors enjoy government-provided insurance in case their bank fails, but only up to $250,000 per account. That could make them leery of handing large sums over to any but the safest institutions. IntraFi's reciprocal network automatically splits and swaps deposits above the cap among member banks, creating linked accounts that each qualify for full insurance coverage. Lenders can then offer more protection to customers, paying a fee to IntraFi for the privilege. Agents could replicate that service on the customer end, sparing humans the labor of opening and tracking balances among multiple accounts. The threat is theoretical at this point. IntraFi's value is, in part, in retaining a single point of contact: a business can act as if they just work with one lender, which they might engage with for a range of services. On their own, a client would also have to do a lot of account-juggling to cover big sums. A number of banks, including JPMorgan (JPM.N) , have said they would restrict agents' access. As with any technology, though, improvements and rapid adoption would make it harder to keep saying no. A sale near the $10 billion target would suggest confidence that this won’t happen. Add on $4.8 billion of debt, according to S&P Global Ratings, and the price would equate to about 24 times IntraFi’s $630 million of annual EBITDA, as reported by Reuters. Given Blackstone's initial $2.5 billion investment in 2019 and nearly $3 billion of dividends along the way, it simplistically implies an over-400% increase in value. Regulatory loopholes are not easily closed, even by frontier technology. Follow Stephen Gandel on LinkedIn and X . Reuters [USN:L6N4651A1 TEXT:"reported"] on October 20 that Blackstone and Warburg Pincus had hired investment banks Morgan Stanley and Guggenheim Securities to find a buyer for IntraFi. The private equity firms are trying to sell their stakes for a combined $10 billion, according to the report. The company, which Blackstone acquired in 2019 for $2.5 billion, dominates the market for reciprocal deposits, which enable banks to spread their customers' money across multiple institutions in order to access federally backed insurance on balances exceeding $250,000. Warburg Pincus purchased a portion of Blackstone's IntraFi stake in 2022 for an undisclosed amount. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s designated first citizen
item.description: The Facebook founder doesn’t hide his admiration for Roman Emperor Augustus. An agreement allows him to sell new non-voting stock to pay a tax bill. Doing so, gives him a larger purse to pursue bigger dreams of conquest while retaining absolute control. Caveat emptor applies.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cyran
item.content:encoded: Mark Zuckerberg has never hid his obsession with Rome and emperor Augustus. A new agreement keeps Meta Platforms’ (META.O) first citizen in the $1.8 trillion company’s capital of Menlo Park, California for eight years. It also allows the founder, chairman and chief executive to pursue bigger dreams of conquest while retaining absolute control. Zuckerberg has some 60% of the company's vote because of Class B shares, which have 10 votes a piece. Yet his economic stake is far less at around 14%. A proposed California tax would hit billionaires like Zuckerberg for 5% of their wealth. He told Meta’s board he might move out of the Golden State, according to the New York Times. It’s understandable directors want the boss in California. Under his leadership, the Facebook and Instagram operator has grown from start up to one of the most valuable companies on earth. Zuckerberg’s focus may be on Meta’s big push into artificial intelligence, but having a leader around the office still delivers better results according to a study by researchers at Boston College and Arizona State University. The company will issue one non-voting Class C share for each existing share investors have. Zuckerberg can sell up to 20% of his immediately, and the remainder in steps, without reducing his voting power. In exchange he stays put instead of relocating out of state. It’s not obvious that Zuckerberg would actually move, let alone leave the company. His desire for retaining power reflects his care for the entity he built. The new shares will be useful for many things. Meta can use them to buy rivals, compensate workers, or raise money to invest in data centers. The company will need this ability, as its artificial intelligence push chews up resources. On Wednesday, the company said it burned over $2 billion in cash in the third quarter. Shareholders have revolted before. In 2017 the company abandoned an attempt to issue non-voting stock. What’s different today is the expensive race to dominate machine learning. Perhaps the opportunity is so big, and the increasing number of tech giants with non-voting stock like SpaceX (SPCX.O) , that equity owners will play along. Rome’s history, though, is hardly an endorsement of letting one person hold absolute power. If things start to go wrong, Meta’s ruler can essentially ignore plebeian investors. Follow Robert Cyran on Bluesky . Meta Platforms said on October 21 that the board had approved a new class of non-voting stock. All Class A and B owners would be issued one new Class C share for each share held. Founder, Chief Executive and Chair Mark Zuckerberg agreed to a deal wherein he can sell up to 20% of his Class C shares in exchange for a commitment to stay in California and remain head of the company for eight years. If he sells more of the shares, his voting stake will be reduced. The restriction on his remaining Class C shares will be lifted in steps over this period. Zuckerberg has a 60% voting stake and owns just over 13% of all shares. The company also reported third quarter results on October 21. In the three months ending September 30, the company had $2.1 billion of negative free cash flow. Meta’s stock fell 6% in early trading on the morning of October 22. CONTEXT-NEWS
